seoTitle: How to Upload Images in GoDaddy Website Builder
metaDescription: Learn how to upload images and add photos in GoDaddy Website Builder, optimize them for speed, and manage your media library with ease.
intro: Good visuals make a real difference for a blog, business site, or portfolio, and GoDaddy Website Builder makes adding them fairly straightforward once you know where to look. This guide covers uploading photos into sections, customizing layouts, and optimizing images so your site loads quickly and looks sharp on any device.

steps.heading: Open the section you want to add an image to
steps.body: Navigate to the page and section in GoDaddy Website Builder where you want a new photo to appear.

steps.heading: Upload your image
steps.body: Use the built-in upload tool to add a photo from your device directly into the section or media library.

steps.heading: Customize the layout
steps.body: Adjust sizing, positioning, and cropping so the image fits well within your page's design.

steps.heading: Optimize for speed and responsiveness
steps.body: Make sure images are appropriately sized and optimized so your site stays fast and looks good on both desktop and mobile.

steps.heading: Manage your media library
steps.body: Keep your uploaded photos organized in the media library so you can reuse or swap them easily later.

faq.question: Can I edit photos directly in GoDaddy Website Builder?
faq.answer: Yes, you can apply basic visual edits to images directly within the builder after uploading them.

faq.question: Will large images slow down my GoDaddy site?
faq.answer: Unoptimized images can slow load times, so it's worth optimizing photos for faster loading and better responsiveness.

faq.question: Where are my uploaded photos stored?
faq.answer: Uploaded images are kept in your media library, which you can browse and reuse across your site.

faq.question: Is this suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, this guide is aimed at beginners who want to enhance their GoDaddy website using the built-in visual tools.
